<steelman>
Centralizing every fix in `lint-fix-loop.sh` by widening `--site` would reuse one battle-tested loop (tmpdir wiring, `LINT_FIX_STATUS`, delta paths, and the existing three-attempt driver in `run_checks_with_lint_fix_loop`) instead of growing another parallel orchestration surface in `ship-pr.sh`.
</steelman>
<claim>
For per-job CI remediation, `ship-pr` should call the same `run_ci_fix_vendor` Cursor→Codex→Claude waterfall, passing each captured local job log as `--failure-log`, and should not extend `lint-fix-loop.sh`’s `--site` enum for that purpose.
</claim>
<evidence>
In [`scripts/ship-pr.sh`](scripts/ship-pr.sh), `run_ci_fix_vendor` iterates tiers `cursor`, `codex`, `claude` and, when a redacted capture exists, passes `--failure-log` into each launcher’s `--role fix` invocation (`1375:1397:scripts/ship-pr.sh`). In contrast, [`scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh`](scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh) frames the task as making `scripts/relevant-checks.sh` pass from a checks log (`40:48:scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh`), and its usage string hard-limits `--site` to `step3|step5|step6|ship-pr-ci-initial|ship-pr-ci-merge` (`22:23:scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh`), which matches the post-vendor `run_checks_with_lint_fix_loop` path (`813:829:scripts/ship-pr.sh`) rather than arbitrary GitHub Actions job output.
</evidence>
<strongest_concession>
Widening `--site` could keep all “LLM fixes repo from a log file” flows behind one script, reducing the chance that a new per-job path diverges from session-env, redaction, or commit-staging conventions that `lint-fix-loop.sh` already encodes.
</strongest_concession>
<counter_to_opposition>
Those conventions are still needed after a vendor fix—`run_ci_fix_vendor` already ends by calling `run_checks_with_lint_fix_loop` for exactly that relevant-checks-shaped pass (`1437:1439:scripts/ship-pr.sh`)—so per-job CI log repair belongs in the launchers that already advertise `--failure-log` for fix roles (`32:32:scripts/launch-cursor-ci.sh`, `28:28:scripts/launch-codex-ci.sh`, `31:31:scripts/launch-claude-ci.sh`), not by overloading a prompt whose success criterion is wired to `relevant-checks.sh`.
</counter_to_opposition>
<risk_if_wrong>
If the waterfall is wrong here, fixes that only make sense against full Actions metadata would misfire on trimmed local-job logs, wasting tiers and still landing in `BAIL_REASON=ci-local-unfixable:…` without improving the PR, while a tailored `lint-fix-loop` site might have steered the model with job-specific instructions.
</risk_if_wrong>
